milestone.title: mp autopilot lane-notification wire format — shell-command, never printed text

intent.outcome: Every lane (orchestrator, runner, reviewer) sends its lifecycle report to the orchestrator pane via a hardcoded shell command invocation of `herdr agent prompt <orchestrator-pane-id>`; a missing shell command in the notification is rejected as a protocol violation by the orchestrator's parser before any state mutation happens.

problem.description: Lesson 1 from the project log (recurring across M200 cycle 1, M201 cycle 1, M202 cycle 1): opencode agents interpret 'notify the orchestrator' as 'print the message' by default. M201's runner fabricated a 'lifecycle=executed' notification; M200's runner printed instead of executing. The fix is structural: the lane-notify prompt template renders the literal `herdr agent prompt ...` command, not the prose, and the orchestrator's parser refuses any notification that lacks a parseable shell-command envelope. This is independent of C2's verifier (which catches state-level lies); C1 catches the *form* of the message — that it was actually sent as a shell command, not printed.

in_scope: Define the lane-notify wire format in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/prompts/lane_notify.rs`: each role template emits a `herdr agent prompt <orchestrator-pane-id> "<role>: cycle N done. ACs: <passed>/<total>. Findings: <list|none>. State: lifecycle=<lifecycle>,execution=<execution_status>."` shell command. The template is per-role (O, R, V).

Parser in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/lane_notify.rs`: parses incoming notifications into a typed `LaneReport` (role, cycle, acs_passed, acs_total, findings, state_snapshot). Rejects messages lacking the `<role>: cycle N done.` prefix or the `State: lifecycle=...,execution=...` line as a protocol violation.

Render-side contract: the role's spawn-prompt (from B2) includes a `Boundaries` block stating 'send your notification by EXECUTING this command, not by printing it'; the lane-notify template is the only path to send.
Regression tests: reproductions of M200 cycle 1 (notification printed but not sent) and M201 cycle 1 (lifecycle claim with no executor-state evidence) — both fail without the fix.
out_of_scope: The orchestrator's state-verification cross-check (mp show milestone + reviews.json + activity.json) — that's C2.
The actual cycle-flow sequencing — that's C3.
Per-AC evidence restoration — that's a separate small track item, not part of C1.

acceptance_criteria.description: The task-assignment wire format (orchestrator → lane) renders correctly per role-direction pair (orchestrator→runner; orchestrator→reviewer). Golden-file tests pin each rendered shell command. The lane→orchestrator notification protocol from prior drafts is removed: lanes now communicate state via session.json writes (B2 + E), not via outgoing prompts.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Lesson-1 enforcement: a task rendered as text (no `herdr agent prompt <lane> "..."` shell form) is rejected as a TaskAssignmentShapeViolation by the orchestrator's command-shape check. Catches both the M200 cycle 1 lesson (printed instead of executed) and any drift where the task template accidentally produces prose instead of a command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Regression — the M200 cycle 1 lesson in task-assignment form: a fake orchestrator that renders a task as text and forwards it via `herdr agent prompt <lane> ""` (empty quoted text, no actual shell command) is detected by the verifier and produces a typed TaskAssignmentShapeViolation error. Reproduces the original failure with the new IPC focus.

design_decisions.choice: Single-line shell command with key=value pairs in the message body, parsed by a hand-rolled parser.
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids JSON-in-shell-command parsing pitfalls (escaping, quoting); agents can compose the message with simple string interpolation, parser stays trivial.

design_decisions.choice: Parser returns a typed error; the orchestrator's state machine (C3) decides whether to resend (3-pane) or escalate (2-pane/1-pane) per the topology-aware decision in B1.
design_decisions.rationale: Separates parsing from decision-making; C1 only owns parsing.
